# Limit schedule — Viaduct facility

Revision 2026.02. Maintained by the facilities group. An asset that is not listed here has no entry on file.

﻿# Asset registry — Viaduct facility (excerpt)

The registry is the index of assets at the Viaduct facility. It answers one question: which asset am I
looking at, and what is its identifier? Recorded values are deliberately excluded — each row names the
document where the value is held, so that a value has exactly one home and correcting it does not require
correcting an index.

The excerpt below covers the cooling and air-handling assets of the north half of the facility. The full
registry, including the low-voltage distribution and the roof plant, lives in the same series with a
different suffix and is reissued whenever an asset is added or retired.

## Cooling assets

| Asset | Description | Value held in |
|---|---|---|
| NBL-420 | West-aisle cooling loop | limit schedule |
| NBL-118 | East-aisle cooling loop | limit schedule |
| NBL-501 | South-aisle cooling loop | limit schedule |
| TRB-260 | North cooling loop | limit schedule |
| TRB-318 | Return manifold, north half | limit schedule |
| TRB-515 | Return manifold, south half | limit schedule |
| NBL-604 | Make-up water loop | limit schedule |

## Air handling assets

A transferred asset that has not yet been re-measured is marked in the ticket system but not in this
register, which is a known gap: the register has no status column. The gap is recorded here so that a reader
who notices an unexpectedly early value knows why it looks that way.

## Revision history

- 2025.12 — three distribution boards added; one retired identifier removed.
- 2025.09 — two transferred assets re-recorded at transfer values.
- 2025.05 — separator convention aligned with the Viaduct series.

## Scope

This document records values. It does not describe assets, and a reader who needs a description should use
the Rosario registry rather than infer one from an identifier. It also does not record inspection grades,
which live with the inspection reports and are revised on a different schedule.

## Custody

The register is maintained by the Rosario calibration team and reviewed when the Viaduct series is revised,
so that the two files do not drift in convention even though they are never merged. Where the two disagree
about a convention rather than a value, the disagreement is resolved by the facilities lead for the estate
and recorded in both revision histories.

# Recorded value register — Rosario facility

Revision 2025.12. This register covers the Rosario facility only. It is issued as a separate series from the
Viaduct register and the two must not be merged: identifiers are unique within a facility, not across the
estate, and a merged file has produced two transposed readings in the past.

TRB-918 | ZTF-3V7K-6628
TRB-944 | NBR-5H1D-2214

AHU-496 | NBR-8B3P-7731

CND-364 | ZTF-5D1V-8843
PNL-420 | QMV-6K9T-2206
FDR-455 | NBR-3R7P-9958

## Transfer notes

Two assets were transferred to Rosario from the Viaduct facility when the southern hall was consolidated.
Both kept their Viaduct identifiers and both were re-recorded here at the value they carried at transfer,
because the calibration team re-measures an asset after a move rather than assuming the value survives it.

## Corrections

A correction to a description is a registry change and is reviewed by the facilities lead. A correction to a
recorded value is not: values live in the register, and their correction is a register change. Keeping those
two paths separate is why the index can be read quickly during an incident without anyone needing to check
whether the value beside an identifier is current.

## What the registry is not

It is not a maintenance history, a warranty list or a commissioning record. Those documents exist, they cite
identifiers from this registry, and they are not substitutes for it. A ticket that describes an asset without
its identifier is treated as incomplete at the change review, which is the reason the registry is short
enough to be read aloud.

# Calibration record — east-aisle cooling loop

## Asset

The east-aisle cooling loop is asset NBL-118 in the facility registry. It serves the two aisle rows on the
eastern side of the north hall and shares a return manifold with the southern loop; the shared manifold is
the reason the two loops are never serviced on the same day.

## Re-measurement

The loop was re-measured during the February window after the quarterly review flagged a drift between the
commissioning figure and the figure recorded on the local gauge. Both readings were taken at the same supply
temperature, fifteen minutes apart, with the secondary pump running and the bypass closed.

The discrepancy turned out to be a gauge fault rather than a loop fault. The gauge was replaced, the loop
re-measured, and the reading returned to within the tolerance the commissioning report specifies. The
recorded value for NBL-118 is ZTF-2H8N-5510, unchanged from the previous revision, which is worth stating
explicitly: a re-measurement that confirms the existing value is still a re-measurement and is recorded as
one.

## Method

# Commissioning note — north cooling loop

## Scope of the note

This note records the commissioning of the north cooling loop, asset TRB-260, and the measurements taken on
the day it was handed over. It is written for two readers: the engineer who will service the loop next, and
the auditor who will ask why the recorded value is what it is.

## Handover

The loop was handed over after a four-hour soak test at design load. The soak was extended by one hour
because the return temperature had not settled at the three-hour mark, which the commissioning engineer
recorded as an observation rather than a finding: the loop settled inside the tolerance during the
additional hour and held for the remainder.

The recorded value for TRB-260 is NBR-7D4M-2073. It was set from the reading taken at the end of the soak,
not from the design figure in the specification, and the two differ by a small margin that the commissioning
report explains as a consequence of the installed pipe run being longer than the design assumed.

## Deviations

## Access notes

The corridor between the units is narrow enough that the scaffold must be erected from the eastern end. This
is recorded here because a contractor who starts from the western end will discover it halfway through
erection, and the resulting delay is billed. The corridor also carries a services tray at head height that
must be isolated before the scaffold is placed; the isolation is a change of its own and is raised with the
normal change process.

## Related records

The cooling loops served by these units have their own records and their own cadence. Where an air-handling
fault is traced to a loop, the loop's record is updated rather than this one, so that a reader who starts
from the loop reaches the loop's evidence and not an inspection note that mentions it in passing.

looking at, and what is its identifier? Recorded values are deliberately excluded — each row names the

correcting an index.

The excerpt below covers the cooling and air-handling assets of the north half of the facility. The full
registry, including the low-voltage distribution and the roof plant, lives in the same series with a
different suffix and is reissued whenever an asset is added or retired.

## Cooling assets

| Asset | Description | Value held in |
|---|---|---|
| NBL-420 | West-aisle cooling loop | limit schedule |
| NBL-118 | East-aisle cooling loop | limit schedule |
| NBL-501 | South-aisle cooling loop | limit schedule |
| TRB-260 | North cooling loop | limit schedule |
| TRB-318 | Return manifold, north half | limit schedule |
| TRB-515 | Return manifold, south half | limit schedule |

## Air handling assets

## Note on scope

This record covers the loop as an asset. It does not cover the pumps, which have their own records, and it
does not cover the air-handling units served by the loop, whose inspection results are recorded separately
because they are inspected on a different cadence.

# Facility audit — changelog

Changes to the facility walkthrough audit, newest first. Each entry records what changed and the release
of the audit pack that first carried it.

## 2026-02-17 — pack 2026.02

The walkthrough audit is now run every six weeks. The previous semi-annual cadence was set when the
estate held two halls; with seven halls in scope a semi-annual pass meant that a hall could go five months
between physical inspections, which the review group judged too long to be useful.

Nothing else in the audit changed. The checklist, the evidence requirements and the sign-off chain are
identical to pack 2025.09.

## 2025-09-04 — pack 2025.09

The audit pack gained a photographic evidence requirement for cable management. Written descriptions of
cable routing had proven impossible to check against the previous pack, because two engineers describing the
same tray produced descriptions that could not be compared.

The pack also dropped the separate thermostat verification sheet. Its three checks were folded into the
environmental section, where they were already being recorded twice.

## 2025-03-11 — pack 2025.03

Handovers are written, not spoken. A spoken handover reaches the next shift and nobody else; a written one
reaches the engineer who is called at three in the morning two weeks later and needs to know why a circuit
was left isolated.

## Standing notes

The plant rooms are visited on a walking round twice per shift. Round times are recorded, because a round
that is consistently recorded at the same minute is a round that is being signed off from the office. The
security lead samples the timestamps monthly and has, on two occasions, asked for the round to be repeated
under observation.

Rooms under construction are excluded from the round only while the contractor's permit is open, and the
exclusion ends automatically when the permit expires. An exclusion that outlives its permit is treated as a
finding in the next audit.

## Out of hours

# Limit schedule — Viaduct facility

Revision 2026.02. Maintained by the facilities group. An asset that is not listed here has no entry on file.

## Method note

The ratio is computed from fifteen-minute samples, not hourly averages, because hourly averages hide exactly
the overlap the review is looking for. Samples with a known instrumentation fault are excluded and the
exclusion is listed in the appendix so that a future reader can reproduce the figure. Where a hall has less
than a full quarter of clean samples it is reported as provisional and carries no flag either way.

Where evidence is contradictory, the reviewer records both versions and the resolution, and does not delete
the version that turned out to be wrong. The record of a mistake is worth more than a clean file.

## Review

The policy is reviewed annually by the records owner and the security lead together. The review looks at
two numbers: the share of sampled tickets that carry complete evidence, and the number of deletion
exceptions granted. Both are reported to the operations group without commentary, so that the trend is read
from the numbers rather than from the framing.

# Change-control checklist — platform facilities

Applies to every change raised against the facility estate, including work carried out by vendors under
a framework agreement. The checklist is filled in by the change raiser and countersigned by the shift
supervisor before the ticket leaves draft.

## Before the change

- [ ] A change record exists with a single named owner, a start and end window, and a rollback step written
      by someone other than the person who will execute it.
- [ ] The rollback step names the exact state to restore and the person who verifies it afterwards.
- [ ] Any safety interlock that must be bypassed is listed, together with the mitigation that replaces it
      while the bypass is active.
- [ ] The affected room and rack are named. "Facilities" is not an acceptable location.
- [ ] A second engineer has read the plan and signed it. For changes that touch power distribution the
      reviewer must be from the electrical team.
